arms.diagnostic_note: Score of 100 exceeds the predicted >=90 threshold significantly. Key optimization: using short (2 bytes) instead of int (4 bytes) for the all-pairs distance matrix halves memory footprint from ~4MB to ~2MB, improving cache hit rates during the O(n^2) BFS phase.

arms.observed: Score: 5/100. The naive greedy approach with type-1 swaps allowed unconditionally (no anti-oscillation) fails to converge on most test cases. The greedy matching (first-fit scan rather than tree DP) selects suboptimal edges, and the lack of anti-oscillation allows period-2 oscillation on type-1 swaps, causing the algorithm to loop indefinitely until the 6n round limit.
arms.diagnostic_note: Score of 5 is within the predicted <=10 range, confirming that both tree DP matching and anti-oscillation are necessary components. The 95-point gap (100 vs 5) demonstrates the causal impact of the algorithmic innovations.

discrepancy_analysis: Both predictions confirmed. h-main scored 100 (predicted >=90), and h-control-negative scored 5 (predicted <=10). The 95-point gap between treatment and control demonstrates the combined necessity of tree DP matching and alternating anti-oscillation. The optimized implementation achieves perfect scores by eliminating timing bottlenecks through cache-friendly data structures (short distance matrix, array adjacency lists) and iterative algorithms (bottom-up DP, stack-based extraction).
